rows: Owner: "can't we just use officially supported otlp stuff?" The `ureq` `HttpClient` adapter in `log_export.rs` is removed; the official `opentelemetry-otlp` exporter now uses its bundled blocking `reqwest` client (native roots), on a thread of its own. Same wire format (OTLP/JSON). Interleaved n=5 rounds x 10 runs of `wf log emit` against a local HTTPS ingest: release binary 8,381,240 B before, 8,457,848 B with the adapter, 8,468,248 B now (+86,008 B vs before); wall 10.39 ms / 10.14 ms / 10.24 ms; peak RSS 22,248 KB in all three; 0 failures of 50 per binary. Deploy-profile binary 10,957,440 to 11,141,256 B. Record `docs/audits/benchmarks/wf-otlp-sdk-official-client.json`. Verification: `wf` unit tests (`log_export` 4, caveat golden on the wire), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, the whole `wf` black-box suite 1,186 of 1,186 in 88 files, none skipped on the clean run (two earlier runs under load skipped the ten Chromium-backed `auth-listener` cases once and failed one `browser-state` case once; each passes alone, 39 of 39 and 12 of 12 three times). Behaviour change: `wf log emit` honours the proxy variables of the environment instead of always connecting directly.
